ai.description: This 3–4 cm frog is olive-brown with dark dorsal mottling and a pale belly. It is distinguished by a prominent, white-tipped snout and distinct, thickened glandular folds along its flanks.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Nanorana blanfordii* is best distinguished by the presence of distinct, prominent glandular folds on its back, which are absent or less developed in similar *Nanorana* species.
ai.habitat: Blanford's frog inhabits high-altitude Himalayan streams and surrounding moist forests, typically found at elevations between 1,500 and 3,000 meters.
ai.behavior: Blanford's frog is primarily nocturnal and exhibits a unique defensive strategy by remaining motionless to blend into the rocky, stream-side environments it inhabits.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Nanorana blanfordii* breeds during the monsoon (June–August), laying small clutches of pigmented eggs attached to submerged rocks in fast-flowing mountain streams.
ai.distributionRemarks: Nanorana blanfordii occurs in the Himalayas across India (Himachal Pradesh to Arunachal Pradesh), Nepal, and Bhutan, typically at elevations between 1,500 and 3,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Nanorana blanfordii* consists of a series of low-pitched, pulsed croaks, typically heard near fast-flowing mountain streams in its habitat.
